items.q: Which column number is the column with the letters ZZZ?
rationales: 17576 is 26 cubed, the number of three-letter columns; ZZZ is the last of them and comes after the 702 columns of one and two letters, so it is 702 + 17576 = 18278.
702 is the column ZZ, with two letters.

items.q: A sheet is read into rows = [['Name', 'Age'], ['Alice', '30']]. Which list position holds the cell B2?
rationales: Cells count from 1 and lists from 0, so the row and the column are both one less than the cell's numbers.
Row 2 is rows[1] and column B is item 1, not 2.

items.q: A cell holds no text. What does int(row[4]) do when row[4] is the empty string ''?
options: It raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
rationales: int of an empty string is an error and not 0; the audit program of the chapter stops on a blank row for that reason.
int never returns None.

items.q: ss.sheetTitles is the tuple ('Sheet1', 'Spam', 'Eggs'). What does ss.sheetTitles[0] = 'X' do?
options: It raises TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment
It inserts a sheet called X
rationales: A tuple is immutable, so nothing is renamed; a sheet is renamed by assigning to its own title.
Assignment to a tuple item never inserts anything.

items.q: A script writes 100 cells of one column, first with 100 single-cell writes and then with one updateColumn call. How many web requests do the two ways make?
rationales: Each single-cell write is its own request, which is what makes a long loop slow and quota-hungry.
updateColumn sends its whole list in one request, so it is not 100.

items.q: The audit program runs on the rows [('PRE-MINE', 'Alice', '1000'), ('Alice', 'Bob', '300')]. What are the balances?
rationales: The pre-mined 1000 goes to Alice and the transfer takes 300 from her and gives it to Bob.
Alice is reduced by the transfer, so it is not 1000.

items.q: addBoringcoinTransaction.py checks len(sys.argv) < 4 and then runs sender, recipient, amount = sys.argv[1:]. What happens for python addBoringcoinTransaction.py Al Sweigart Eve 2000, without quotes?
options: It adds a transaction from 'Al Sweigart' to 'Eve'
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3, got 4)
rationales: Without quotes the shell makes four arguments, Al, Sweigart, Eve and 2000, not three.
There are five items in sys.argv, which is not fewer than 4, so the usage message is not printed.

items.q: In EZSheets 2026.4.28, what does a quota error from Google do when ezsheets.IGNORE_QUOTA is True?
options: The HttpError is raised at once
The request is retried after growing pauses, nine attempts in all, and then the HttpError is raised
The request is dropped without an error
rationales: That is what the chapter says, but in this library the setting only switches off the library's own throttle, and the retry stays.
The library raises the error in the end and never drops a request silently.

items.q: Why must a token-sheets.pickle file from another person never be loaded with pickle.load?
options: The file is too large to load
Unpickling can run code chosen by whoever made the file
Pickle files are encrypted and cannot be read
rationales: Size is not the issue; the danger is in what loading does.
A pickle file is not encrypted; it is a recipe for building objects, and the recipe can call functions.

items.q: Which scope does Google's scope table recommend when access to only the files an app itself uses is enough?
rationales: The Drive scope is classed as restricted and gives access to all of the user's Drive files.
The Sheets scope is classed as sensitive and covers all the user's spreadsheets.

items.q: A script has loaded a sheet. Someone changes cell A1 in the browser. What does sheet['A1'] show in the script before sheet.refresh() is called?
options: The old text, read from the script's loaded copy
rationales: The script does not see the change until it refreshes.
Reading the loaded copy is not an error.
